sutta: Nidana Samyutta 12.70. That's what I heard. On occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Rajagaha in this bamboo grove, the squirrel sanctuary. On that occasion the Blessed One was honored, respected, esteemed, venerated and revered. He obtained robes, alms food, lodgings and medicinal requisites. The bhikkhu sangha too was honored, respected, esteemed, venerated and revered. And the bhikkhus or the monks too obtained robes, alms food, lodgings and medicinal requisites. But the wanderers of other sects were not honored, respected, esteemed, venerated and revered. And they did not obtain robes, alms food, lodgings and medicinal requisites. Now, on that occasion the wanderer Susima was residing in Rajagaha along with a large company of wanderers. Then his company said to the wanderer Susima, "Come, friends, Susima, lead the holy life under the ascetic Gotama. Master his Dhamma and teach it to us. We will master his Dhamma and preach it to the lay people. Thus, we too will be honored, respected, esteemed, venerated and revered. And we too will obtain robes, arms, food, lodgings, and medicinal requisites. All right, friends, the wanderer Susima replied. He then approached the venerable Ananda and exchanged greetings with him. When they had concluded their greetings and cordial talk, he sat down to one side and said to him, friend Ananda, I wish to lead the holy life in this Dhamma-Vinaya. Then the venerable Ananda took the wanderer Susima approach and approached the Blessed One. He paid homage to the Blessed One, and then he sat down to one side and said to him, venerable sir, this wanderer Susima says that he wishes to lead the holy life in this Dhamma-Vinaya. Well, then Ananda, give him the going forth. The wanderer Susima then received the going forth and the higher ordination under the Blessed One. Stop here for a moment. So, you see this uh external sect wanderers, they saw that the Buddha and his disciples were getting a lot of offerings. Whereas they were getting very few offerings. So, they thought must be because the people like the Buddha's Dhamma. So, if they also learn the Buddha's Dhamma, they will also get a lot of offerings. So, they asked Susima to go and learn the Dhamma. On that occasion, a number of monks had declared final knowledge in the presence of the Blessed One saying, we understand destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. The venerable Susima heard about this. So, he approached those monks, exchanged greetings with them, and then sat down to one side and said to them, is it true that you venerable ones have declared final knowledge in the presence of the Blessed One saying, we understand destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being. "Yes, friend." They replied. And then he said, "Then knowing and seeing thus, do you verbal ones wield various kinds of spiritual psychic power, such that having been one, you become many. I mean, one body, you multiply into many bodies. Having been many, you become one. You appear and vanish. You go unhindered through a wall, through a rampart, through a mountain as though through space. You dive in and out of the earth as though it were water. You walk on water without sinking, as though it were earth. Seated cross-legged, you travel in space like a bird. With your hand, you touch and stroke the moon and sun, so powerful and mighty. You exercise mastery with the body as far as the Brahma world." Let's stop here for a moment. Yes, "Exercise mastery with the body as far as the Brahma world" means with the flesh body, yeah, they can fly as far as the Brahma world, the first Jhana heavens, and not further. And then they replied, "No, friend." No, they don't have all this psychic power. Then he said, "Then knowing and seeing thus, do you verbal ones with the divine ear element, which is purified and surpasses the human, hear both kinds of sounds, the divine and human, those that are far as well as near?" And they said, "No, friend." "Then knowing and seeing thus, do you verbal ones understand the minds of other beings and persons, having encompassed them with your own minds? You understand a mind with lust as a mind with lust, a mind without lust as a mind without lust, a mind with hatred as a mind with hatred, a mind without hatred as a mind without hatred, a mind with delusion as a mind with delusion, a mind without delusion as a mind without delusion, a contracted mind as contracted, and a distracted mind as distracted, and an exalted mind as as exalted, and an unexalted mind as unexalted, a surpassable mind as surpassable, and an unsurpassable mind as unsurpassable, a concentrated mind as concentrated, and an unconcentrated mind as unconcentrated, a liberated mind as liberated, and an unliberated mind as unliberated. And they said, "No, friend." So, here, he is asking them, "If you don't have all the various types of psychic powers, you have the divine ear, the heavenly ear?" Surely, and they said, "No." And they said, "Now, if you don't have that, maybe you have the ability to read other people's minds?" And they also said, "No." Then, knowing and seeing thus, do you, venerable ones, recollect your manifold past of births, that is, one birth, two births, three, four, five, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 100 births, 1,000, 100,000 births, many eons of world contraction, many eons of world expansion? Many eons of world contraction and expansion thus, "There I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such was my experience of pleasure and pain, such my lifespan. Passing away from there, I was reborn elsewhere, and there too, I was so named, of such a clan, with such an appearance, such was my food, such my experience of pleasure and pain, such my lifespan. Passing away from there, I was reborn here." Do you thus recollect your manifold past of births with their modes and details? "No, friend," they replied. So, he's asking them whether they can see their past lives, and still they say, "No." Then, knowing and seeing thus, do you, venerable ones, with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, see beings passing away and being reborn, inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings fare on in accordance with their karma. Thus, these beings who engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, who reviled the noble ones, the Ariyans, held wrong view and undertook actions based on wrong view. With the breakup of the body after death, have been reborn in a state of misery, in a bad destination, in the nether world, in hell. But, those beings who engaged in good conduct of body, speech, and mind, who did not revile the noble ones, who held right view, and undertook action based on right view. With the breakup of the body after death, have been reborn in a good destination, in a heavenly world. Thus, with a divine eye, which is purified passes the human, you see beings passing away and being reborn, inferior and superior, beautiful and ugly, fortunate and unfortunate, and understand how beings fare on in accordance with their karma. No, friend. So, here he's asking them whether they have the divine eye. Heavenly eye, and they also said, "No." How come he's asking all these questions? Uh probably because one of the reasons the Buddha and the disciples have become so uh famous and receive so much support is because people know they have all these psychic powers. Then he said, "That knowing and seeing thus, do you venerable ones dwell in those peaceful deliverances that transcend forms, the formless attainments, having touched them with the body?" And they said, "No, friend." We'll stop here for a moment. So, here the the last part he's asking uh whether they have attained the uh states of meditation. Where uh the formless attainments, that means uh they have passed beyond form the arupa jhanas, they have attained the arupa jhanas. In meaning the base of boundless space, the base of boundless consciousness, the base of nothingness, the base of neither perception or non-perception. These are the four arupa jhanas which are the very high states of meditation. And they say also say no. Then he said, "Here now venerable ones, this answer and the non-attainment of those states, how could this be, friends?" And they said, "We are liberated by wisdom, friend Usuma." And he said, "I do not understand in detail, friends, the meaning of what has been stated in brief by the venerable ones. It would be good if the venerable ones would explain to me in such a way that I could understand in detail what has been stated in brief." And they said, "Whether or not you understand, friend Usuma, we are liberated by wisdom." I'll stop here for a moment. So here he's asking them like uh you all claim that you have attained uh the goal of the holy life, you have become liberated from the round of rebirths and all that. But how is it when I ask you all these states, psychic powers and all that, you you you say you don't have all these? Then they said, "That's because we are liberated by wisdom." And they asked them to explain and they refused to explain. Earlier we read some some sutta where it was mentioned that there were there were group of arahants and the Buddha said uh I think the group was 500 arahants and the Buddha said 60 of them have the threefold knowledge, 60 of them have the sixfold knowledge, 60 of them are liberated by mind or two ways liberated and and the rest are all liberated by wisdom. So out of these 500, you see 100 120 have the threefold knowledge and the sixfold knowledge, which means psychic power. So, 120 out of 500 is about 1/4. So, about 1/4 of arahants after they become liberated now only 1/4 have psychic power. 3/4 generally don't have psychic power. Though here they they say they don't have psychic power and they are liberated by wisdom. This is Sutta like this that the commentary makes a mistake. The commentary says that this refers to this means that the arahants who are liberated by wisdom who don't have psychic power means that they don't have any jhana. They equate jhana with psychic power. They think once a person attains jhana, he must have psychic power. So, these arahants don't have psychic power, therefore they don't have jhana. But here the last part they ask they have not attained the formless janas, arupa janas, but in other suttas the Buddha says to attain arahanthood you must have at least the four janas. The four janas are enough to make a person an arahant if he studies the Dhamma also in in addition to the four janas. And if he attains the arupa janas is a bonus, but it's not a necessary condition. That's the mistake the commentaries make. From here they talk about the pure vipassana arahant which does not need any jhana. This totally contradicts the suttas. The Buddha said in the Majjhima Nikaya that it's impossible to destroy the five lower factors without the four janas. Person who destroys the five lower factors is the anagami and the arahant. Then the venerable Susima rose from his seat and approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One, sat down to one side, and reported to the Blessed One the entire conversation he had had with those monks. The Blessed One said, "First, Susima, comes knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma. Afterwards, knowledge of Nibbana." Stop here for a moment. So, here the Buddha is saying, "First, a person has knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma." Has knowledge basically means a person has knowledge of the Dhamma. Then, because of knowledge of the Dhamma, he has knowledge of Nibbana. That means he gains liberation. And Susima said, "I do not understand in detail, venerable sir, the meaning of what was stated in brief by the Blessed One. It would be good if the Blessed One would explain to me in such a way that I could understand in detail what has been stated in brief." And the Buddha said, "Whether or not you understand, Susima, first comes knowledge of the stability of the Dhamma. Afterwards, knowledge of Nibbana." And the Buddha continued, "What do you think, Susima, is form or body permanent or impermanent?" "Impermanent, venerable sir." "Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?" "Suffering, venerable sir." "Is what is impermanent suffering and subject to change fit to be fit to be regarded thus, 'This is mine. This I am. This is myself'?" "No, venerable sir." "Similarly, is feeling permanent or impermanent?" And he answered as before. "Is perception permanent or impermanent? Is volition permanent or impermanent? Is consciousness permanent or impermanent?" He answered all in the same way. "Impermanent, venerable sir." "Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?" "Suffering, venerable sir." "Is what is impermanent suffering and subject to change fit to be regarded thus, "This is mine, this I am, this is myself." No, venerable sir. Stop here for a moment. So, here the Buddha is teaching him in some Dhamma. Buddha is asking him about the five aggregates, uh body, feeling, perception, volition, and consciousness. Which these five things are basically body and mind. Which we take to be the self or as belonging to the self or the self is in these five aggregates or the five aggregates are in the self. So, the Buddha is trying to make him see that these these five aggregates which we take to be the self is impermanent. So, it is suffering and it's not fit to be regarded as I or mine. And the Buddha continued, "Therefore, Susima, any kind of form whatsoever, whether the past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, all form or bodies should be seen as it really is with correct wisdom thus, "This is not mine, this I am not, this is not myself." So, here when we talk about all forms means our body uh whether our body now or body in the past or our bodies in the future or those the bodies that we take to be mine like my uh husband, my wife, my children, my parents, and all that. Uh the Buddha said that all these you should see with wisdom. This is not mine, this I am not, this is not myself. Similarly, any kind of feeling whatsoever, any kind of perception, any kind of volition, any kind of consciousness whatsoever, whether past, future, or present, internal or external, gross or subtle, inferior or superior, far or near, all these aggregates are be seen as it really is with correct wisdom does. This is not mine. This I am not. This is not myself. Seeing does to see my instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards all, revulsion towards feeling, revulsion towards perception, revulsion towards volition, revulsion towards consciousness. Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion, his mind is liberated. When it is liberated, there comes the knowledge. It is liberated. He understands destroyed his birth. The holy life has been lived. What had to be done has been done. There is no more for this state of being. So here the Buddha makes him understand this Dhamma. And then the Buddha continued, "You see Sushima, with birth as condition, heating and death comes to be." Yes, venerable sir. "You see Sushima, with exist with being as condition uh birth." And he says, "Yes." "You see with with clinging as condition existence etc." "Contact and six sense bases etc. With ignorance as condition, volition comes to be." And he says, "Yes, venerable sir." to all of this. "You see Sushima, with cessation of birth comes cessation of aging and death." "Yes, venerable sir." "You see Sushima, with cessation of being comes cessation of birth." "Yes." Similarly, with the cessation of clinging etc. Cessation of ignorance comes cessation of volition. To all this he says, "Yes, venerable sir." So here the Buddha is trying to make him see dependent origination of suffering and dependent cessation of suffering. Now, basically, after he has stayed with the Buddha for some time, he would have learned all this from the other monks. But here the Buddha is is uh explaining to him to to him see uh this uh basic Dhamma which makes a person become liberated. And then the Buddha said, "Knowing and seeing thus, O Susima, do you wield the various kinds of spiritual power such that having been one, you become many, etc., etc., and exercise bodily mastery as far as the Brahma world?" So, here the Buddha is saying uh since you understand all these Dhamma, uh then do you have all these uh various types of psychic power, because psychokinesis? And he says, "No, venerable sir." "Then knowing and seeing thus, O Susima, do you with the divine ear element, which is purified and surpasses the humans, hear both kinds of sounds, the divine and human, those that are far as well as near?" And he said, "No, venerable sir." "Then knowing and seeing thus, O Susima, do you understand the minds of other beings and persons, having encompassed them with your own mind?" "No, venerable sir." "Then knowing and seeing thus, O Susima, do you recollect your manifold past births with their modes and details?" "No, venerable sir." "Then knowing and seeing thus, O Susima, do you with the divine eye, which is purified and surpasses the human, see beings passing away and being reborn and understand how beings fare on in accordance with their karma?" "No, venerable sir." "Then knowing and seeing thus, O Susima, do you dwell in those peaceful deliverances that transcend forms, the formless attainments, having touched them with the body?" And he said, "No, venerable sir." And then Buddha said, "Hear now, Susima, this answer of yours and the non-attainment of those states, how could this be, Susima?" Uh so, let's stop here for a moment. So, the Buddha is repeating exactly what he said earlier, lah. He asked the arahants since they have understood the Dhamma and become liberated, how come they don't have all the psychic powers? So, the Buddha is also uh making it making him understand that that having understood all this Dhamma, why is it that you also don't have any psychic power? Then the venerable Susima prostrated himself with his head at the Blessed One's feet and said, "Venerable sir, I have committed a transgression in that I was so foolish, so confused, so inept that I went forth as a thief of the Dhamma in such a well expounded Dhamma Vinaya as this. Venerable sir, may the Blessed One pardon me for my transgression, seeing as a transgression for the sake of future restraint." And the Buddha said, "Surely, Susima, you have committed a transgression in that you were so foolish, so confused, so inept that you went forth as a thief of the Dhamma in such a well expounded Dhamma Vinaya as it is. Suppose, Susima, they were to arrest a bandit, a criminal, and bring him before the king saying, 'Sire, this man is a bandit, a criminal. Impose on him whatever punishment you wish.' King would say to them, 'Come, men, bind this man's arms tightly behind his back with a strong rope, shave his head, and lead him around from street to street and from square to square beating a drum. Then take him out through the southern gate and to the south of the city cut off his head.' What do you think, Susima, would that man experience pain and displeasure on that account? Yes, venerable sir." And the Buddha said, "Although that man would experience pain and displeasure on that account, going forth as a thief of the Dhamma in such a well expounded Dhamma Vinaya as this has results that are far more painful, far more bitter, and further, it leads to the nether world. But since you see your transgression as a transgression and make amends for it in accordance with the Dhamma, we pardon you for it. For it is growth in the noble one's discipline when one sees one's transgression as a transgression, makes amends for it in accordance with the Dhamma and undertakes future restraint. That's the end of the Sutta. So, here you see, yeah, this Susima, having learned the Dhamma, he realized that he uh did something very wrong and uh he asked for forgiveness. He understood that when a person sees the Dhamma, it's not necessary that he has all these psychic powers. powers, but you see, for him to confess to the Buddha shows uh that he has understood the Dhamma, shows that I believe that he has at least attained stream entry. So, having attained stream entry, yeah, he realized how good the Dhamma is, then only he admitted to the Buddha. You know, you see that he he says uh "I have committed a transgression in a in that I was so foolish to confuse. I went forth as a thief of the Dhamma in such a well-expounded Dhamma-Vinaya as this." So, he realized that the Buddha's Dhamma-Vinaya is so perfect, so good, and he is so bad. So, at least he has become stream enterer and he won't go back to his old friends in the external Sangha. And if he strove only, could have become an Arahat. Now, we come to that's the end of the Nidana Samyutta. We took the Samyutta talks, took us about six talks. Maybe five and a half. Now, we come to the second chapter of the Nidana book. It's the 13th chapter, 13th Samyutta of the whole Samyutta Nikaya. It's called the Abhisamaya Samyutta. It's discourses uh connected to the topic on the breakthrough to the Dhamma. People who understood have understood the Dhamma and attained stream entry. They how the the benefit now of it now.
